غَيْلَمٌ : see غَلِمٌ. ―
-b2- Also A beautiful woman. (TA.) ―
-b3- And A youth, or young man, broad, (K, TA,) in the M large, (TA,) in the place of the parting of the hair of the head, having much hair; (K, * TA;) as also ↓ غَيْلَمِىٌّ . (Lth, K, TA.) ―
-b4- مَا بِالدَّارِ غَيْلَمٌ means [There is not in the house] any one. (K.) ＝
-A2- Also The tortoise: (TA:) or the male tortoise. (S, K, TA. [In the Msb said to be, in this sense, غَلِيم, like زَبِيب.]) ―
-b2- And The frog. (K.) [Or so عَيْلَمٌ.] ＝
-A3- And The place whence issues the water in wells. (K. [See also عَيْلَمٌ.]) ＝
-A4- The word signifying “ a comb, ” and “ a [thing with which the head is scratched, called] مِدْرًى, ” is فَيْلَم, with ف, but has been mistranscribed [غَيْلَم], (K, TA,) by Lth, as has been notified by Az. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
